drivers.why_material: Company maintained 'on track for mid-2022' guidance in May 2022 when the registered primary completion date of April 2022 had already passed, after a pattern of repeated slippage from 2020-09 → 2021-03 → 2021-06 → 2021-10 → 2022-04. This is about the catalyst trial (FORWARD, wAIHA, Phase 3).
Duplicate finding of rigl_001 from same document, reinforcing the 'on track' claim when registered timeline had already been missed. Same catalyst trial.

In January 2022, company guided to mid-2022 when the registered primary completion date of October 2021 had already passed by three months, continuing a pattern of slippage without transparent acknowledgment. Same catalyst trial.
Duplicate finding of rigl_012 from same document, maintaining mid-2022 guidance despite passed October 2021 registered date. Same catalyst trial.

analyst_note: Rigel repeatedly claimed the FORWARD wAIHA Phase 3 trial was 'on track' for mid-2022 data even as registered completion dates slipped multiple times (from Sept 2020 through April 2022) and had already passed when the claims were made. In January 2022, they guided to mid-2022 when the ClinicalTrials.gov date of October 2021 was three months overdue; in May 2022, they maintained 'on track' when the April 2022 registered date had lapsed. While all findings are graded minor severity individually, the pattern of maintaining rosy guidance while registered timelines slip and pass suggests operational-execution issues the company is not transparently disclosing. This does not rise to a company-level fraud tell, but represents a non-dismissible masking signal specific to the catalyst trial that warrants elevated caution.
